```{r lib, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(car)

```

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```



## Step 1: LOAD, SELECT, AND RENAME CORE COLUMNS
```{r Step1}
df_raw <- read.csv("PlayerValueData.csv")

# Select and rename all necessary columns (including those needed for calculation)
df_working <- df_raw %>%
  # Select and rename columns (R automatically converts spaces to dots)
  select(
    Market_Value = Value, Age, Position, League, 
    Total_Minutes = Min..20.21., Total_90s = Total.Mins.90..20.21.,
    Goals_90 = Gls.90..20.21., Assists_90 = Ast.90..20.21.,
    # Select the raw counts needed for calculating per-90 rates later
    Raw_Tackles = Total.Number.of.Players.Tackled..20.21.,
    Raw_Interceptions = Total.Interceptions..20.21.
  )
```
## Step 2: CLEANING AND RELIABILITY FILTERING
```{r Step2}
# Drop rows missing critical performance metrics
df_working <- df_working %>%
  drop_na(Total_Minutes, Goals_90, Raw_Tackles, Raw_Interceptions)

# Filter for reliable per-90 statistics (at least 400 minutes played)
df_working <- df_working %>%
  filter(Total_Minutes >= 400)

# Check remaining size (Should be 1594 rows)
print(paste("Rows after cleaning and reliability filtering:", nrow(df_working)))
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.



## Step 3: FEATURE ENGINEERING
```{r Step3}
# 3.1 Create the Major_Position factor variable
df_working <- df_working %>%
  mutate(
    Major_Position = case_when(
      str_detect(tolower(Position), "attack") ~ "Forward",
      str_detect(tolower(Position), "midfield") ~ "Midfielder",
      str_detect(tolower(Position), "defender") ~ "Defender",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    # 3.2 CALCULATE final per-90 defensive metrics (The Missing Step!)
    Tackles_90 = Raw_Tackles / Total_90s,
    Interceptions_90 = Raw_Interceptions / Total_90s
  ) %>%
  # Remove 'Other' positions (Goalkeepers, etc.)
  filter(Major_Position != "Other")

# Check remaining size (Should be 1594 rows)
print(paste("Rows after position filter and feature engineering:", nrow(df_working)))
print("Position Distribution:")
print(table(df_working$Major_Position))
```
## Step 4: FINAL SELECTION, FACTORING, AND SAMPLING
```{r Step4}
df_final_clean <- df_working %>%
  select(
    Market_Value, Age, Major_Position, League, Total_Minutes, 
    Goals_90, Assists_90, Tackles_90, Interceptions_90
  )
# Convert necessary columns to factors
df_final_clean$Major_Position <- as.factor(df_final_clean$Major_Position)
df_final_clean$League <- as.factor(df_final_clean$League)

# Set the Seed for Reproducibility (Crucial for the final report!)
set.seed(42) 

# Randomly sample down to exactly 900 rows (The final project data set)
df_final_900 <- df_final_clean %>%
  sample_n(size = 900, replace = FALSE)

# Check the final structure
print(paste("Final Analytical Data Set Size:", nrow(df_final_900), "rows."))
str(df_final_900)

# Save this final file for submission alongside your R script
write.csv(df_final_900, "soccer_player_value_cleaned_project_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
## Q.1 - What factors predict a player's market value?(MLR)
```{r Q.1}
df_final_900 <- df_final_900 %>%
  mutate(Log_Market_Value = log(Market_Value)) # Create the new column
model_best <- lm(
  Log_Market_Value ~ Goals_90 + Assists_90 + Tackles_90 + Interceptions_90 +
    Age + log(Total_Minutes) +
    League ,
   data = df_final_900
)
summary(model_best)
vif(model_best)
```
  
  
## Q.2 - Do Positions Have Different Market Values? (ANOVA)
```{r Q.2}
anova_model <- aov(Market_Value ~ Major_Position, data = df_final_900)
summary(anova_model)

TukeyHSD(anova_model)

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df_final_900, aes(x = Major_Position, y = Market_Value, fill = Major_Position)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Market Value Distribution by Position",
       x = "Position",
       y = "Market Value") +
  theme_minimal()
```



## Q.3 - League vs High-Value Players (Chi-square Test)
```{r Q.3}
 df_final_900 <- df_final_900 %>%
  mutate(High_Value = ifelse(Market_Value > 10000000, 1, 0))
table(df_final_900$League, df_final_900$High_Value)

chisq.test(table(df_final_900$League, df_final_900$High_Value))
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(df_final_900, aes(x = League, fill = as.factor(High_Value))) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(title = "Proportion of High-Value Players by League",
       x = "League",
       y = "Proportion",
       fill = "High Value (1 = Yes)") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  theme_minimal()

```


## Q.4 - Define “Versatile Player” Based on Stats(MLR) and OR(odds ratio)
```{r Q.4}
df_final_900 <- df_final_900 %>%
  mutate(
    Versatile = ifelse(
      Goals_90 >= quantile(Goals_90, 0.50) &
        Assists_90 >= quantile(Assists_90, 0.50) &
        Tackles_90 >= quantile(Tackles_90, 0.50),
      1, 0
    )
  )

vers_model <- glm(
  Versatile ~ Age + Total_Minutes + Major_Position,
  data = df_final_900,
  family = "binomial"
)

summary(vers_model)
exp(coef(vers_model))
exp(confint(vers_model))


df_final_900 <- df_final_900 %>%
  mutate(
    Versatility_Score = 
      scale(Goals_90) * 0.4 +
      scale(Assists_90) * 0.3 +
      scale(Tackles_90) * 0.3
  )
ggplot(df_final_900, aes(x = Goals_90 + Assists_90, y = Tackles_90 + Interceptions_90)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, aes(color = Major_Position)) +
  labs(
    x = "Attacking Contribution",
    y = "Defensive Contribution",
     title = "Identifying Versatile Players"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


## Q.5 - Young talent using two sample proportion test
```{r Q.5}
df_final_900 <- df_final_900 %>%
  mutate(Young = ifelse(Age < 23, 1, 0))

df_two_leagues <- df_final_900 %>%
  filter(League %in% c("Premier League", "La Liga"))
df_two_leagues <- df_two_leagues %>%
  droplevels()

table(df_two_leagues$League, df_two_leagues$Young)
prop.test(table(df_two_leagues$League, df_two_leagues$Young))

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(df_two_leagues, aes(x = League, fill = as.factor(Young))) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(
    title = "Young Player Proportion (<23) in EPL vs La Liga",
    x = "League",
    y = "Percentage of Young Players",
    fill = "Young (1 = Yes)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


## Q.6 - Aging Star Discount Analysis
```{r Q.6}
df_final_900 <- df_final_900 %>%
  mutate(Attacking_90 = Goals_90 + Assists_90)

att_median <- median(df_final_900$Attacking_90, na.rm = TRUE)

df_high_att <- df_final_900 %>%
  filter(Attacking_90 >= att_median)

model_age_discount <- lm(
  Market_Value ~ Age + Attacking_90,
  data = df_high_att
)

summary(model_age_discount)

df_high_att <- df_high_att %>%
  mutate(
    Age_Group = cut(
      Age,
      breaks = c(-Inf, 22, 26, 30, Inf),
      labels = c("U23", "23-26", "27-30", "31+")
    )
  )

group_means <- df_high_att %>%
  group_by(Age_Group) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_Attacking_90 = mean(Attacking_90, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_Market_Value = mean(Market_Value, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

print(group_means)

u23_values <- df_high_att$Market_Value[df_high_att$Age_Group == "U23"]
old_values <- df_high_att$Market_Value[df_high_att$Age_Group == "31+"]

t_test_age <- t.test(u23_values, old_values, var.equal = FALSE)
t_test_age

# Q.6b - Does the discount survive controls? The t-test above is a raw
# difference; it does not adjust for league, position, minutes or output.
df_high_att <- df_high_att %>% mutate(Age_Group = relevel(Age_Group, ref = "U23"))
model_age_controlled <- lm(
  log(Market_Value) ~ Age_Group + Attacking_90 + League + Major_Position + log(Total_Minutes),
  data = df_high_att
)
summary(model_age_controlled)
# % difference in value vs U23, holding the controls fixed (31+ is about -81%)
exp(coef(model_age_controlled)[grep("Age_Group", names(coef(model_age_controlled)))]) - 1

# Is the discount specific to high performers? Age x output interaction on all 900.
model_interaction <- lm(
  log(Market_Value) ~ Age * Attacking_90 + League + Major_Position +
    log(Total_Minutes) + Tackles_90 + Interceptions_90,
  data = df_final_900
)
summary(model_interaction)   # Age:Attacking_90 is not significant (p ~ 0.74)

ggplot(df_high_att, aes(x = Age, y = Market_Value)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Aging Star Discount: Market Value vs Age\n(High Attacking Players)",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Market Value (Euro)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
## Q.7 - Overrated or Underrated

```{r Q.7}

summary(model_best)

df_final_900$Pred_Log_Value <- predict(model_best, newdata = df_final_900)
df_final_900$Predicted_Value <- exp(df_final_900$Pred_Log_Value)
df_final_900$Residual <- df_final_900$Market_Value - df_final_900$Predicted_Value
df_final_900$Residual_z <- as.numeric(scale(df_final_900$Residual))
top_undervalued <- df_final_900 %>%
  arrange(Residual_z) %>%
  head(10)

top_undervalued
top_overvalued <- df_final_900 %>%
  arrange(desc(Residual_z)) %>%
  head(10)

top_overvalued

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(df_final_900, aes(x = Predicted_Value, y = Market_Value, color = Residual_z)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
  scale_color_gradient2(
    low = "blue",
    mid = "grey80",
    high = "red",
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "Residual Z-Score"
  ) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Hidden Bargains Index: Predicted vs Actual Market Value",
    x = "Predicted Market Value (Model-Based)",
    y = "Actual Market Value",
    subtitle = "Points below dashed line are undervalued; above line are overvalued"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
